content.personal_data: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable natural person ('data subject'); an identifiable natural person is one who can be identified, directly or indirectly, in particular by reference to an identifier such as a name, an identification number, location data, an online identifier or to one or more factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that natural person
content.processing: Any operation or set of operations which is performed on personal data or on sets of personal data, whether or not by automated means, such as collection, recording, organisation, structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation, use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction
content.data_subject: The natural person to whom personal data relates
content.controller: The natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which, alone or jointly with others, determines the purposes and means of the processing of personal data
content.processor: A natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body which processes personal data on behalf of the controller
content.sub_processor: A processor engaged by the processor to carry out specific processing activities on behalf of the controller
content.data_breach: A breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data transmitted, stored or otherwise processed
content.supervisory_authority: An independent public authority which is established by a Member State pursuant to Article 51 of the GDPR

content.subject_matter: This Data Processing Agreement (DPA) forms part of the main agreement between the Controller and the Processor for the provision of services and governs the processing of personal data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller.
content.duration: This DPA shall remain in effect for the duration of the main agreement and for such period as the Processor continues to process personal data on behalf of the Controller.
content.termination: Upon termination of the main agreement or this DPA, the Processor shall cease all processing of personal data and shall return or delete all personal data in accordance with the provisions of this DPA.

content.purpose: The Processor shall process personal data solely for the purposes specified in the main agreement and as instructed by the Controller from time to time.
content.scope: The processing activities shall include but not be limited to: data collection, storage, analysis, reporting, and any other processing activities necessary for the provision of the agreed services.
content.restrictions: The Processor shall not process personal data for any other purpose without the prior written consent of the Controller.

categories: Personal identification information (names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers)
Professional information (job titles, company information, work contact details)
Technical data (IP addresses, device information, usage data)
Any other categories of personal data as specified in the main agreement
content.special_categories: The Processor shall not process special categories of personal data unless explicitly authorised by the Controller and in compliance with Article 9 of the GDPR.
content.data_minimization: The Processor shall ensure that only personal data that is necessary for the specified purposes is processed.

categories: Customers and clients of the Controller
Employees and contractors of the Controller
Any other categories as specified in the main agreement
content.rights: Data subjects shall have all rights granted to them under the GDPR, including but not limited to the right of access, rectification, erasure, and data portability.

obligations_and_rights.title: Obligations and Rights of the Controller

controller_obligations: The Controller shall be responsible for ensuring that it has a legal basis for the processing of personal data
The Controller shall provide clear and specific instructions to the Processor regarding the processing of personal data
The Controller shall ensure that data subjects are informed about the processing of their personal data
The Controller shall respond to data subject requests in accordance with the GDPR
controller_rights: The Controller shall have the right to audit the Processor's compliance with this DPA
The Controller shall have the right to receive breach notifications from the Processor
The Controller shall have the right to approve or reject sub-processors
The Controller shall have the right to terminate processing activities
The Controller shall have the right to receive processing records and compliance information

content.processing_instructions: The Processor shall process personal data only on documented instructions from the Controller, including regarding transfers of personal data to a third country or an international organisation.
content.confidentiality: The Processor shall ensure that persons authorised to process personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.
content.security_measures: The Processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.
content.assistance: The Processor shall assist the Controller in responding to requests for exercising the data subject's rights.
content.breach_notification: The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
content.deletion_or_return: The Processor shall delete or return all personal data to the Controller after the end of the services relating to processing, and delete existing copies unless Union or Member State law requires storage of the personal data.
content.compliance_demonstration: The Processor shall make available to the Controller all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations laid down in Article 28 of the GDPR.
content.audit_assistance: The Processor shall allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the Controller or another auditor mandated by the Controller.

technical_measures: Encryption of personal data at rest and in transit using industry-standard encryption algorithms
Access controls and authentication mechanisms to ensure only authorised personnel can access personal data
Regular security assessments and penetration testing to identify and address vulnerabilities
Incident detection and response procedures to quickly identify and respond to security incidents
Data backup and disaster recovery procedures to ensure data availability and integrity
Network security measures including firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and secure network architecture
organisational_measures: Staff training on data protection and security best practices
Confidentiality agreements for all personnel who have access to personal data
Physical security controls to protect data processing facilities
Incident response and business continuity planning
content.specific_measures: The Processor shall implement additional security measures as specified in the main agreement or as required by the nature of the personal data being processed.

content.authorisation: The Processor shall not engage another processor without prior specific or general written authorisation of the Controller.
content.sub_processor_obligations: The Processor shall impose the same data protection obligations on any sub-processor by way of a contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law.
content.liability: The Processor shall remain fully liable to the Controller for the performance of any sub-processor's obligations.
content.notification: The Processor shall inform the Controller of any intended changes concerning the addition or replacement of other processors, thereby giving the Controller the opportunity to object to such changes.
content.sub_processor_list: The Processor shall maintain an up-to-date list of sub-processors and make it available to the Controller upon request.

right_of_access.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain confirmation as to whether or not personal data concerning them is being processed, and, where that is the case, access to the personal data and information about the processing.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall assist the Controller in responding to access requests
The Processor shall provide the Controller with the requested personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format
The Processor shall maintain records of all access requests and responses

right_to_rectification.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain the rectification of inaccurate personal data concerning them.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall assist the Controller in rectifying inaccurate personal data
The Processor shall notify any sub-processors of rectifications made
The Processor shall update processing records to reflect rectifications

right_to_erasure.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain the erasure of personal data concerning them without undue delay.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall assist the Controller in erasing personal data
The Processor shall ensure erasure from all systems, backups, and sub-processor systems
The Processor shall provide certification of erasure to the Controller

right_to_data_portability.description: Data subjects have the right to receive personal data concerning them in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall assist the Controller in providing data in a portable format
The Processor shall ensure data is provided in a machine-readable format
The Processor shall maintain data structure during portability operations

right_to_restriction.description: Data subjects have the right to obtain restriction of processing where certain conditions are met.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall implement processing restrictions as instructed by the Controller
The Processor shall maintain data during restriction periods
The Processor shall notify the Controller before lifting restrictions

right_to_object.description: Data subjects have the right to object to processing of personal data concerning them.
processor_obligations: The Processor shall cease processing upon objection unless the Controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds
The Processor shall assist the Controller in evaluating objections
The Processor shall implement processing stops as instructed by the Controller

content.notification_timeline: The Processor shall notify the Controller without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after becoming aware of a personal data breach.
notification_content: The nature of the personal data breach including, where possible, the categories and approximate number of data subjects concerned and the categories and approximate number of personal data records concerned
The likely consequences of the personal data breach
The measures taken or proposed to be taken by the Processor to address the personal data breach, including, where appropriate, measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects
The contact details of the data protection officer or other contact point where more information can be obtained
processor_obligations: The Processor shall document all personal data breaches, comprising the facts relating to the personal data breach, its effects and the remedial action taken
The Processor shall assist the Controller in notifying the supervisory authority of the breach
The Processor shall assist the Controller in communicating the breach to data subjects where required
The Processor shall cooperate with the Controller in any investigation of the breach
content.escalation: If the Processor is unable to provide all required information within 72 hours, the notification shall be made in phases without undue further delay.

content.audit_frequency: The Controller shall have the right to conduct audits of the Processor's compliance with this DPA on an annual basis or upon reasonable request.
audit_process: The Controller may conduct audits directly or appoint a third-party auditor
The Processor shall provide reasonable assistance and access to relevant personnel, systems, and documentation
Audits shall be conducted during normal business hours with reasonable notice
The Processor shall bear the costs of its own participation in audits
Audit results shall be shared with the Processor and any remedial actions shall be implemented within an agreed timeframe
content.documentation: The Processor shall maintain comprehensive documentation of all processing activities and make it available for audit purposes.

termination_grounds: Breach of the obligations of this DPA by the Processor
Legal or regulatory requirements that prevent continued processing
Termination of the main agreement between the parties
post_termination_obligations: The Processor shall cease all processing of personal data immediately upon termination
The Processor shall return or delete all personal data in its possession or control
The Processor shall provide certification of deletion to the Controller
The Processor shall maintain confidentiality obligations after termination
The Processor shall assist the Controller in data portability if requested
survival_clauses: Audit rights for compliance verification shall survive termination
Dispute resolution procedures shall survive termination
content.data_retention: The Processor shall not retain any personal data after termination unless required by law, and shall provide the Controller with a detailed retention schedule if such retention is necessary.

content.governing_law: This DPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the jurisdiction specified in the main agreement.
content.jurisdiction: Any disputes arising out of or in connection with this DPA shall be subject to the jurisdiction of the courts specified in the main agreement.
content.gdpr_compliance: This DPA is designed to ensure compliance with the GDPR and shall be interpreted in accordance with GDPR requirements.
content.conflict_resolution: In the event of any conflict between this DPA and the main agreement, the provisions of this DPA shall prevail with respect to data protection matters.

content.processor_liability: The Processor shall be liable to the Controller for any damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of the GDPR specifically directed to processors or where it has acted outside or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.
content.indemnification: The Processor shall indemnify and hold harmless the Controller from and against any claims, damages, losses, or expenses arising from the Processor's breach of this DPA or applicable data protection laws.
content.limitation_of_liability: The liability provisions of the main agreement shall apply to this DPA, subject to any mandatory provisions of applicable data protection law.
content.joint_liability: Where the Processor, together with other processors, is involved in the same processing and where, in accordance with paragraphs 1 and 2, they are, under civil law, responsible for any damage caused by the processing, each processor shall be held liable for the entire damage in order to ensure effective compensation of the data subject.

content.escalation: Any disputes arising under this DPA shall first be escalated to senior management of both parties for resolution.
content.mediation: If escalation does not resolve the dispute, the parties shall attempt to resolve the matter through mediation before pursuing legal action.
content.arbitration: If mediation is unsuccessful, disputes shall be resolved through binding arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause in the main agreement.
content.regulatory_complaints: Nothing in this DPA shall prevent either party from making complaints to supervisory authorities or seeking judicial remedies as provided for under the GDPR.

content.definition: Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance under this DPA due to circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to acts of God, war, terrorism, riots, fire, natural disasters, government actions, or other similar events.
content.notification: The party affected by force majeure shall notify the other party promptly of the occurrence and expected duration of the force majeure event.
content.obligations: During a force majeure event, the Processor shall continue to implement appropriate security measures to protect personal data to the extent reasonably possible.
content.termination: If a force majeure event continues for more than 30 days, either party may terminate this DPA with immediate effect.
